newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ERA confident on Jabiluka, uranium.
newsitem.headline: ERA confident on Jabiluka, uranium.

text.p: Energy Resources of Australia Ltd was hopeful that its major new Northern Territory uranium mine Jabiluka would go ahead, chief executive Phillip Shirvington told Reuters on Monday.

Speaking after an address to a uranium conference here, Shirvington said approval for Jabiluka was not anticipated before the end of 1997 but ERA hoped to be in production at the end of 1999 or early year 2000, Shirvington said.

The new mine, in Kakadu national park in the Northern Territory, would increase group production of uranium oxide by 1,000 tonnes a year to 6,000 tonnes. Production is now being expanded to 5,000 tonnes a year at the existing Ranger mine, 20 kilometres south of Jabiluka.

ERA is presently in the process of public consultation and producing an environmental statement on Jabiluka, the biggest of several new Australia uranium mines likely to be brought into production. ERA is 68 percent owned by North Ltd.
Shirvington also forecast that uranium oxide spot prices would settle in the long term at US$15 to US$18 a pound in real terms.
This would compare with present prices of slightly less than US$14 a pound after a slight decline from a peak of US$16.50 in April last year.
World uranium prices are recovering from a slump after hitting a low of US$7.75 a pound in 1992.
